About

The person who keeps the details from slipping

I'm an operations and administrative support professional from the Philippines with over three years of experience behind the scenes of a multi-branch business.

My day job was purchase orders, supplier and branch coordination, inventory and sales tracking, record checks and relentless follow-up. I checked quantities against NetSuite and Excel so mismatches were caught before they became billing or stock problems.

I'm now applying the same habits to property management support. The maintenance, CRM and bookkeeping projects are simulated workflows that show how I'd organize requests, follow-ups and records. Each is clearly labeled as a sample.

How I work

Every request follows the same path to done

  1. Understand

    I clarify what's needed, who's involved and what "done" looks like.

  2. Organize

    Details go into a tracker, CRM record or ticket so nothing lives in someone's head.

  3. Coordinate

    I contact the tenant, vendor, supplier or teammate and confirm times and approvals.

  4. Follow up

    I monitor pending items and chase delays before they become complaints.

  5. Close

    I document the outcome and finish the task, or escalate it with the facts in hand.

Sample project · Property maintenance & vendor coordination

Request · HVAC · AC not coolingSAMPLECLOSED · $165

AC is running but the house won't cool

Issue
Tenant reported the AC was running but not cooling.
Action
Confirmed the problem with the tenant, booked the HVAC technician, confirmed access, documented the findings, secured approval for the $165 capacitor replacement and followed up after the repair.
Result
Faulty capacitor replaced. Tenant confirmed normal cooling. Request closed.
See the tenant and vendor conversations
Request · Plumbing · Kitchen sink leakSAMPLECLOSED · $175

Leak under the kitchen sink

Issue
Tenant reported a kitchen sink leak while the faucet was in use.
Action
Collected tenant details, coordinated the plumber's inspection, confirmed the service window, documented the $175 estimate, obtained approval and followed up after the repair.
Result
P-trap connection replaced. Tenant confirmed no more leaking. Final cost $175, invoice received.
Request · Appliance · Refrigerator not coolingSAMPLECLOSED · $210

Fridge and freezer not cooling, part on backorder

Issue
Refrigerator and freezer weren't cooling, with a clicking sound every few minutes.
Action
Coordinated the technician's inspection, confirmed tenant access, tracked the estimate and the replacement part, followed up on the delay, booked the return visit and verified completion.
Result
Compressor start relay replaced. Tenant confirmed normal cooling. Final cost $210.
